cover.html: Introduce the demo. The persona is a workplace or IT operations lead who owns the MIMO room tablets. The data is the tablet registry from a SQL database, collected into Elastic every 15 minutes. The map on the right is drawn from the real city coordinates and tablet counts of the live data. Message: the registry only knew city and country as text, and Elastic turns that into a map.
challenge.html: Frame the challenge. The registry holds country, city, site, building, room, capacity, bookable and app version, but no coordinates. That is enough to list tablets and not enough to draw them, group them by region or plan work by time zone. Ask the audience how they answer 'how many tablets in France, in which building?' today. Expect: an export and a spreadsheet.
how-it-works.html: Walk the four steps left to right. 1: the MIMO SQL registry. 2: Elastic Agent reads it every 15 minutes, one document per tablet. 3: a GeoNames lookup, loaded once with about 208,000 cities, adds coordinates, country code and time zone while the data is collected. 4: Kibana shows the map and dashboard. Use the example strip: Munich, Germany becomes 48.14, 11.57, DE and Europe/Berlin. Stress that nothing changes in the MIMO database and that no external geocoding service is called.
demo-1-estate-map.html: How to present: this is the lead demo, about five minutes. Show the three numbers first: 689 tablets, 41 cities, 18 countries (illustrative figures: replace them with the live dashboard numbers before the meeting). Then switch to the live dashboard: Overview KPIs, then the map. Start at world view with country shading, zoom into Europe where city bubbles and labels appear (Munich, Madrid and London are the largest in the sample). Use the pinned Country filter, for example Germany. Show the Top 20 buildings by room count, then the Latest poll per room table for one room. Avoid the check-in, check-out and environment sections: they hold configuration flags, not live activity. Full demo script: demo/scenario-1-estate-map.md.
demo-2-timezones.html: How to present: second demo, about three minutes. Pain: nobody can tell which offices are open when an update goes out, because the registry has no time zone. The bars show tablets per time zone: Europe/Berlin 174, Madrid 96, Paris 70, down to Australia/Brisbane 3 (8 of 22 zones shown, illustrative figures). In the live dashboard open the Timezone section: 22 distinct time zones and the Tablets by timezone chart. Propose a wave plan: smallest zones first as a pilot, then the largest offices. The time zone comes from the GeoNames enrichment, it does not exist in the source database. Do not promise live local time per office: grouping by zone works today, computing local time was not tested. Full demo script: demo/scenario-2-timezones.md.
closing.html: Close on the value: see the estate, plan by time zone, reuse the lookup for any city and country field. Then raise the next step: alert when a whole office stops reporting. Today the SQL feed reads the registry, so it keeps returning rows even if an office loses its network, and status is almost always INACTIVE. A heartbeat or last-seen signal from the MIMO backend, or network monitoring per office, is needed. Ask who owns the MIMO database.
